candidate: ca0756a plus compact transmit storage, per-lane FIFOs, buffer ownership exchange and bounded source batching
notes: Release x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, opt-level 3, full LTO, stripped, one codegen unit; local Linux 6.8.0-147-generic.

Fresh namespaces and processes per observation except variants marked persistent, which keep the same daemons, TAPs, sockets and namespaces across all rates. No local owned builds or tests overlap load. Socket hash placement can differ across independent observations.
Goodput excludes drain; missing/reordered and drop counters include drain. Process/thread CPU covers load; receiver CPU includes drain.
TAP and socket counters count SKBs; a dropped input source can contain many Ethernet frames. Counters cannot be summed into an exact frame-loss decomposition.
QinQ uses strict hashing; single-tag ordinary UDP retains reader-local lanes. SRv6 has one VLAN, real IPv6-in-IPv6 encapsulation and strict inner-flow hashing.
Rejected global-queue storage prototype caused a severe asymmetric collapse. Per-lane FIFO tests reproduce and fix overtaking of older frames by new arrivals.
Ownership exchange swaps an empty owner buffer for a borrowed reader buffer; no payload copy, larger pool or shorter deadline.
The four-source candidate changes adaptive GSO read batching; owner-batch retains a one-source limit when input needs local expansion. Expansion remains bounded to 64 frames or 64 KiB per turn.
The batch4-generator-seg1 observations use one segment per send and saturate the generators around 1.9 Gbit/s; they are not comparable to 44-segment transport ceilings.
The endflush variant removes intermediate receive delivery and is rejected: its persistent QinQ sweep regressed versus the retained 32-completion threshold.
Single observations do not establish a universal plateau or satisfy the five-run 20 Gbit/s / under-1%-missing gate.
